expected_output.reasoning: The agent correctly advises against simply remounting read-write, explains that EXT4 went read-only as a protective measure against I/O errors, identifies the root cause as a likely EBS volume/hardware issue rather than something yum/dnf can fix, and warns that forcing a remount could worsen corruption or cause an unbootable instance. It proposes the correct next step of checking EBS volume status/health before any remount, consistent with the expected guidance to check describe-volume-status and treat it as a volume issue. While it doesn't explicitly mention snapshot/replace volume or fsck via rescue instance by name, it offers to walk through the proper diagnosis including checking EBS volume status, which aligns with the core expected message: don't just remount; investigate volume health first. The core substance of the expected output is met, though some specific remediation steps (snapshot/replace, fsck/xfs_repair via rescue instance) are only alluded to as part of 'proper diagnosis' rather than spelled out.
